scenes.en: One pair of glasses for far, middle and near.
scenes.say: Holding your phone at arm's length to read it? In this video, we explain progressive lenses: one pair of glasses for far, middle and near vision.

scenes.en: This is called presbyopia. It happens to almost everyone.
scenes.ta: 40 வயதுக்கு மேல் அருகில் உள்ளவை தெளிவாக தெரியாது
scenes.say: After about forty, the lens inside the eye slowly becomes less flexible, so focusing up close gets harder. This is called presbyopia, and it happens to almost everyone.

scenes.en: Single vision, bifocal and progressive.
scenes.say: Once you need help for both distance and near, there are three main choices: single vision, bifocal, and progressive.

scenes.en: One power across the whole lens. Great for one distance.
scenes.say: Single vision lenses have one power across the whole lens. They are great for one distance, but you may need two pairs and keep switching between them.

scenes.en: Two zones with a visible line: distance on top, reading below.
scenes.say: Bifocals have two zones with a visible line: distance on top, and reading below. Middle distances, like a computer screen, can fall in between.

scenes.en: No line. The power changes smoothly from top to bottom.
scenes.say: Progressive lenses have no visible line. The power changes smoothly from the top of the lens to the bottom, so you can see far, middle and near with one pair.

scenes.en: Driving, TV, faces across the room.
scenes.say: Look through the top of the lens for distance: driving, watching TV, or seeing faces across the room.

scenes.en: A narrow corridor for arm's-length tasks.
scenes.say: The middle corridor is for arm's length: your computer screen, the car dashboard, or a shop counter.

scenes.en: Phone, newspaper, price tags.
scenes.say: Lower your eyes to the bottom of the lens to read your phone, the newspaper, or price tags.

scenes.en: Every progressive has some blur at the sides. That's normal.
scenes.say: Every progressive lens has some blur at the lower sides. That is normal. You learn to turn your head, not just your eyes, toward what you want to see.

scenes.en: Fusion progressives: Narrow, Wide, Custom HD and Individual designs.
scenes.say: Progressive designs differ in how wide the clear zones are. At our store, Fusion progressives come in Narrow, Wide, Custom HD and Individual designs. Wider designs give a wider clear view, though the edges are never completely clear. We also offer progressive lenses from leading international brands.

scenes.en: Wear them all day. Point your nose at what you look at.
scenes.say: Most people get used to progressives within a week or two. Wear them all day, point your nose toward what you're looking at, and lower your eyes, not your head, to read.

scenes.en: Look through the top part, not the reading zone.
scenes.say: On stairs, tilt your head down a little, so you look through the distance part, not the reading zone. Hold the handrail at first.

scenes.en: Accurate PD and fitting height put each zone right in front of your eyes.
scenes.say: Good fitting matters most. Your pupil distance and fitting height must be measured carefully, so each zone sits right in front of your eyes. A frame with enough lens height also helps.

scenes.en: Fact: progressives help anyone whose near vision has changed, often from the early 40s.
scenes.say: Myth number one: progressives are only for old people. Fact: they help anyone whose near vision has started to change, which is often in the early forties.

scenes.en: Fact: near focus changes with age anyway. Glasses just help you see clearly.
scenes.say: Myth number two: wearing glasses makes your eyes weaker. Fact: near focus changes with age anyway. Glasses simply help you see clearly and comfortably.

scenes.en: Rinse with water, wipe with a microfibre cloth, keep them in a case.
scenes.say: Take care of your lenses. Rinse them with water, wipe them with a clean microfibre cloth, and keep them in a case, not face down on the table.

scenes.en: Your power can change. Regular eye tests keep every zone accurate.
scenes.say: Your power can keep changing with age, so get your eyes tested every one to two years, or sooner if anything feels different.

scenes.en: Over 40 and juggling two pairs? Get an eye test first.
scenes.ta: இரண்டு கண்ணாடி மாற்றுகிறீர்களா? முதலில் கண் பரிசோதனை
scenes.say: If you are over forty and juggling two pairs of glasses, progressives may suit you. But first, get a complete eye test, so your power is accurate.
